# apple_in_app_purchase_price_points (Data Source)

Reads Apple's catalogue of permitted prices for a one-time in-app purchase.

A price is never a number: `apple_in_app_purchase_price_schedule` references price points, and each price point fixes a customer price and the developer proceeds for one territory. This data source is how you find the ID of the one you want.

**Always set `territories`.** The unfiltered catalogue covers every territory the App Store sells in and runs to tens of thousands of records; the filter is passed to Apple rather than applied in memory, so it is the difference between one request and hundreds. Price point IDs are scoped to the purchase they were read from and cannot be reused on another — nor can a subscription's price points be used here.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "apple_apps" "example" {
  bundle_id = "com.example.app"
}

data "apple_in_app_purchases" "pro_unlock" {
  app_id             = data.apple_apps.example.apps[0].id
  product_id_pattern = "^com\\.example\\.app\\.prounlock$"
}

# Always pass territories. The unfiltered catalogue covers every territory the
# App Store sells in and runs to tens of thousands of records; the filter is
# passed to Apple rather than applied in memory.
data "apple_in_app_purchase_price_points" "usa" {
  in_app_purchase_id = data.apple_in_app_purchases.pro_unlock.in_app_purchases[0].id
  territories        = ["USA"]
}

# Narrow to one price. customer_price is matched exactly, after Apple's
# territory filter -- note that the same number means a different amount of
# money in each territory's currency.
data "apple_in_app_purchase_price_points" "usa_9_99" {
  in_app_purchase_id = data.apple_in_app_purchases.pro_unlock.in_app_purchases[0].id
  territories        = ["USA"]
  customer_price     = "9.99"
}

# Several territories at once, for a schedule that overrides Apple's equalized
# prices across a region.
data "apple_in_app_purchase_price_points" "region" {
  in_app_purchase_id = data.apple_in_app_purchases.pro_unlock.in_app_purchases[0].id
  territories        = ["USA", "GBR", "EGY", "DEU"]
  limit              = 100
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `in_app_purchase_id` (String) The ID of the in-app purchase whose price catalogue to read.

### Optional

- `customer_price` (String) Return only price points whose customer price matches this string exactly, for example `9.99`. Applied in memory after Apple's territory filter. Note that the same numeric price means a different amount of money in each territory's currency.
- `limit` (Number) Maximum number of price points to return. Applied after filtering.
- `territories` (List of String) Three-letter Apple territory codes to restrict the catalogue to, for example `["USA", "GBR", "EGY"]`. Applied by Apple, not in memory. Omitting this returns every territory, which is rarely what you want.

### Read-Only

- `filtered_count` (Number) Number of price points remaining after filtering, before the limit.
- `price_points` (Attributes List) The price points matching the filters. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--price_points))
- `total_count` (Number) Number of price points Apple returned before the in-memory filter.

<a id="nestedatt--price_points"></a>
### Nested Schema for `price_points`

Read-Only:

- `customer_price` (String) What the customer pays, in the territory's currency.
- `id` (String) The price point ID, to be passed to `apple_in_app_purchase_price_schedule`.
- `proceeds` (String) What the developer receives, in the territory's currency.
- `territory_id` (String) The three-letter Apple territory code this price point belongs to.
